# The people of Veyra

Each person's first paragraph is what you know when you meet them. Later paragraphs are revealed as districts are restored, so they are spoilers.

## You, the Keeper

*The hero*

A traveller who came up the coast road with a pack, a walking stick and no clear memory of why. You arrived in Veyra the morning after the worst Tide in three hundred years. The lantern in the Archive warmed in your hands when it would warm for no one else, and nobody, least of all you, knows why.

**After 5 gates (spoiler):** The Hushed have started watching you. Someone tried to kill you in the Clockwork Market, which suggests that somebody in Veyra knows more about you than you do.

**After 10 gates (spoiler):** In a waystation register on the Outer Roads you found your own handwriting, dated a year ago: a courier's mark and a single line, "Delivered to the Archivist. Returned by choice." You have been here before. You came back on purpose. You just do not remember deciding to.

**After 12 gates (spoiler):** You carry the Heartledger. Calder walked it into your memory on the night of the Tide and then took the memory of the walk away, so that no one could torture it out of you. Every palace you have built this year has been you, slowly, finding your way back to it.

## Wren Halloway

*Your companion*

Twenty-seven, junior archivist, daughter of a lamplighter from the Quay. Tall, quick-talking, forever tripping on stairs, with ink on every finger and a long brown coat that has notecards in all eleven of its pockets. She writes everything down because, as a girl, she lost her mother's face to a Tide and has never forgiven herself for it. She is funnier than she lets on and braver than she believes.

**After 2 gates (spoiler):** She has started leaving the cards at home, one pocket at a time. She will not admit that this frightens her, but she checks her empty pockets when she thinks you are not looking.

**After 9 gates (spoiler):** Wren was not a junior clerk. She was Calder's true apprentice, the one meant to carry the Heartledger next. On the night of the Tide, Calder made her drink the grey and forget it, so the Hushed would stop hunting her. The face scratched out of every wall in the Hall of Faces was hers. Calder did it to hide her.

**After 12 gates (spoiler):** Archivist of Veyra, the first in three hundred years to keep the Heartledger without a single notecard. She still carries one card in her breast pocket. It has your name on it, and she says it is not there because she might forget.

## Sevrin Ashgrave, the Grand Hush

*The adversary*

Leader of the Quiet Order. A tall, soft-spoken man in a grey hood, with silver in his beard and a voice that makes people want to sit down and rest. He feeds the poor of the Lower Tiers with his own hands. He has never raised his voice in public. Every report of him agrees on one thing: he seems sincerely kind.

**After 5 gates (spoiler):** Sevrin once had a wife named Marra and a daughter named Lia. Both died in the Red Fever twelve years ago. Afterwards he drank the grey and forgot them, and found, for the first time in his life, peace. He has spent every day since trying to give that peace to everyone else, whether they want it or not.

**After 11 gates (spoiler):** Sevrin Ashgrave was born Sevrin Calder. He is the Archivist's younger brother. He means to open the Lethe Gate on the Night of No Moon and let a Tide like a wall roll over Veyra, so that the whole city wakes the next morning with nothing to grieve. He calls it the Great Mercy.

**After 12 gates (spoiler):** Calder kept one memory he did not know survived: Lia, aged six, laughing on the Quay steps with a paper boat. When you showed it to him at the Gate, he wept for the first time in twelve years, and then he closed the floodgates with his own hands.

## Elsabet Calder, the Archivist

*The vanished mentor*

Archivist of Veyra for thirty-one years. Precise, dry, unbending, famously stingy with praise. She vanished on the night of the great Tide, leaving nothing behind but a cold lantern and a city of blank ledgers.

**After 6 gates (spoiler):** She opened the Lethe Gate herself that night, a hand's width, on purpose. The question that keeps you awake is why.

**After 11 gates (spoiler):** She has been here all along. Old Tansy, the herbalist who makes remembering-tea on the Quay, is Calder: she drank a full cup of the grey on the night of the Tide so the Hushed could never take the city's secrets from her mind. She does not know who she was. She only knows, from somewhere deep, that she must keep an eye on you.

## Joss Hask

*The drifter*

A road-warden from the Outer Roads, six and a half feet tall and broad as a doorway, who walked into Veyra with a folding knife, a spare shirt and a ferry token in his pocket and nothing else. He says very little. He notices everything. When he decides something is wrong, he fixes it, usually before anyone else has finished deciding whether it is wrong.

**After 4 gates (spoiler):** He is hunting the Salt Guild men who sold the grey to his brother. He has a list of their names, which he keeps in his head because, he says, "paper gets found."

## Isolde Varre, the Harbour Mistress

*The intriguer*

Mistress of the Harbour and the richest woman in Veyra. Dark-eyed, sharp-witted, always perfectly dressed, always three moves ahead. She plays cards for high stakes at Varre House and always wins. She saved your life in the Clockwork Market and has not yet told you what she wants for it.

**After 8 gates (spoiler):** She handed you to the Hushed on the Tidal Stair. You thought it was betrayal. It was the only way to get you inside the Order's hall, and she has been Calder's eyes in the Quiet Order for ten years. She still has not told you what she wants. You are beginning to suspect it is simply to win.

## Old Tansy

*The herbalist of the Quay*

A small, sharp old woman with a stall under the last lamp of the Quay, where she sells rosemary tea "for the remembering" and gives advice nobody asked for. Nobody knows how long she has been there. She seems to like you, which surprises everyone, including her.

**After 11 gates (spoiler):** Tansy is Elsabet Calder, the lost Archivist, wiped clean by her own hand. Every cup of tea she pressed on you this year was her way of keeping watch over the one person who carried what she had lost.

## Brother Ennick

*The doubter*

A young acolyte of the Quiet Order, freckled, earnest and badly out of place. He joined the Hushed to forget a cruel father. Then he was set to copying the Order's records, and he began to notice that the records did not agree with each other.

**After 7 gates (spoiler):** He brought you the true account of the night of the Tide, at great risk, and now hides in the Scriptorium cellars. He is trying very hard to remember how to be brave.

## Edrin Halloway

*Wren's father*

A lamplighter of the Quay, who lit lamps twenty-three to forty-four. Quiet, with a bad knee and a house at number thirty-one, Quay Row, whose blue door he has been promising to repaint for twenty years.

**Later (spoiler):** He came to the Amphitheatre to watch his daughter and stayed to give you the things he remembers of his wife's face. He asked you to keep them. "She would want her face to have someone."

**Later (spoiler):** He has finally repainted the door. It is green. He says blue was only ever a mistake he never fixed.

## Marit Halloway

*Wren's mother*

A lamplighter of the Quay who lit lamps one to twenty-two and hummed a tune with no words while she did it. She died in the winter of the long cough, when Wren was eight. The Tide took her face from Wren's memory that same week, an ordinary Tide, and nobody's fault.

## Ambrose Tallow, the Winder

*The last Warden of the Hours*

The Warden who kept the Tide's timetable and wound the Mother Clock. Three hundred years ago he stepped into the Seam to hold one evening in place, and nobody has said his name since. He was not cruel. He was lonely. He paid for the Order's oil and wicks for eleven years without being asked for anything, and he is remembered now: Ambrose Tallow, Warden of the Hours, who kept the last lamp.

## The Keepers' Circle

The friends who coach a Keeper before and after an Echo battle, never during a question. Each joins once their district is restored.

- **Wren**: "Hold the first picture steady before the mist reaches it. I will be right behind you with my cards, though I promise not to peek."
- **Tansy**: "Take a breath of rosemary and hold the first picture, dear. The mist only takes what slips loose, so keep your grip gentle and steady."
- **Fennick**: "Fix each one to its spot, nice and firm, before you answer. That'll hold."
- **Hask**: "Plain hands, clear eyes. One item at a time."
- **Isolde**: "Anchor your images tight, darling. The Tide only takes what slips loose."
- **Mosk**: "Pin the memory down, lad. The Tide eats what you let slip. Keep your feet planted."
- **Ennick**: "Breathe. I have slipped on exactly this kind of thing before, so I know it happens. Steady, and look straight at it."

## The Forgettings

What the Tide leaves behind when it loosens a memory. They do not bite; they wait to be remembered.

- **Smudge** (Visual Association): a blurred picture
- **Tangle** (Story Linking): a loose thread of a story
- **Hollow** (Memory Palace): a room with the furniture gone
- **Blank** (Names and Faces): a face without a name
- **Static** (Number Encoding): a drift of numbers
- **Murmur** (Vocabulary and Concepts): a word on the tip of the tongue
- **Dustleaf** (Structured Knowledge): a page of loose facts
